title: Why Do You Get Shocked by Door Handles in Winter?
short_title: Why Winter Door Handles Shock You (Static Electricity)
description: Ever got a tiny shock from a door handle? Here is the simple science of static electricity and dry winter air.
tags: why do I get static shock
comment: Do you get shocked a lot in winter? Tell me! ⚡

scenes.text: Why do you get a tiny electric shock from a door handle in winter?
Winter air is very dry. In humid air, extra charge leaks away through tiny water drops. In dry air, it stays on you.
When you walk on a carpet, your shoes rub tiny negative charges, called electrons, onto your body.
Then you touch metal, and all those electrons jump across the gap at once. That jump is a tiny lightning bolt.
To reduce it, touch the wall first, use a humidifier, or moisturise your skin.
It is harmless, just a little spark of science.
